w: At 10.00am amidst Vedic chantings Swamishri performed the murti-pratishtha of Akshar Purushottam Maharaj, Radha Krishna Dev, Hanumanji, Ganapatiji and Guru Parampara.

After a four-hour flight, Swamishri landed in Nairobi at 6.00 pm. A welcome assembly was held in the BAPS Swaminarayan Mandir. On the way to the mandir from the airport, Swamishri commented on the lack of greenery in the countryside. The driver informed Swamishri that the country was experiencing a drought. Swamishri prayed, “God will shower His grace. It will rain.”

Despite the heavy rains everywhere, Swamishri was eager to reach New Delhi for the final stages of preparation for the inauguration of Swaminarayan Akshardham. Swamishri left by car from Sarangpur at 4.05 pm and arrived at Bhavnagar airport at 6.00 pm. At 6.20 pm, Swamishri flew to New Delhi, arriving there at 8.20 pm.

At 6.00 pm 2100 dignitaries assembled in the mandir hall for a satsang assembly. Viveksagar Swami addressed them on the subject of true happiness. Thereafter Gnanvatsal Swami talked about the generation gap. A video on Swaminarayan Akshardham was shown. And finally Swamishri blessed the assembly by elaborating upon the boons given by God to man and the importance of satsang in life. Thereafter Swamishri personally blessed all the dignitaries.

To please Bhagwan Swaminarayan and Guru Pramukh Swami Maharaj children, youths and senior devotees perform austerities, pilgrimages or other devotional means. The spiritual endeavors performed by the devotees during Swamishri's visit to the local centers are congratulatory and worthy of recognition. It also reflects Swamishri's divinity for inspiring such spiritual efforts in children, teenagers and devotees.
Darshansingh Sardar pilgrimaged 260 km by foot from Chandigadh to Akshardham. He covered the distance in five days, walking 120 km on the last day. Swamishri blessed him for his effort and faith.

At 10.00 Swamishri arrived at Edison mandir to celebrate the festival of Jal Jhilani Ekadashi. After Thakorji’s darshan and abhishek of Nilkanth Varni, Swamishri walked onto the main stage amidst the joyous applause of thousands of devotees. After the pujan rituals of Shri Harikrishna Maharaj, Swamishri steered a small boat on which Shri Harikrishna Maharaj was standing in a small makeshift pool of water. After performing five artis the head sadhus of each region spoke for a few minutes about the transforming effect of Swamishri’s stay in their centres. Thereafter senior sadhus and devotees garlanded Swamishri. Finally Swamishri blessed the festival assembly, “The festival celebrates the arrival of God after the monsoon rains fill the rivers and reservoirs with fresh, new water. He blesses all with divine joy and happiness. The jiva has to be purged of base instincts and faults. By taking refuge in God one’s ignorance and bad nature are dissolved. He liberates one from maya and blesses with brahmabhav (divinity). He brought the Gunatit Sadhu, whose association frees one from the bondage of mine-ness and infatuation for worldly objects.” At 12.20 pm Swamishri returned to East Brunswick. The next day Swamishri departed by flight from America at 9.35 am and landed at Farnborough airport at 9.10 pm (G.M.T). Swamishri arrived at the Neasden Mandir at 10.15 pm and briefly attended an assembly of devotees. Before retiring at 11.00 pm he blessed all the London sadhus for having fasted for 100 hours. Also, 241 devotees had observed fasts and other austerities.

Jagmal Pithiya, who had come from Vadodara, had so far brought 176 men and women into satsang. He had come with a list of all their names. He said to Pramukh Swami Maharaj, "Please place your hand on this paper, so that satsang takes root in everyone's soul."
Pleased, Swamishri placed his hand on the list, and in this way blessed them all.
In today's daily newspaper 'Divya Bhaskar', Professor Mehboobbhai Desai, an appreciative Muslim, beautifully described what he felt in his heart after Swamishri's darshan in Bhavnagar. He writes:

"It was the 19th roza (fast) of the month of Ramadan. After reading the Fajr namaz (dawn prayer), I sat down to recite the Holy Qur'an. Just then my wife Sabera spoke up, 'Hiteshbhai has invited us to come to Akshardham at about eight this morning. Shall we go?'

The Holy Qur'an says, 'God has sent a guiding scripture and a guide for every community.' That is why, for years, our home has had the custom of respecting every religion and its saints. I said, 'All right, we will go.' Deep in my heart there was a longing to have darshan once again of Pramukh Swamiji of the Swaminarayan Sampradaya, who had come to Bhavnagar at that time. We reached Akshardham at about eight. Hiteshbhai was standing waiting for us right in the mandir premises. He welcomed us. Then he led us towards a large hall. The hall was filled with about five thousand devotees. Sabera took a place in the women's section, while Hiteshbhai and I sat in the men's section. The atmosphere in the hall was full of devotion. Pramukh Swamiji was seated on a large, grand stage. Beautiful bhajans flowed from the microphone, making the atmosphere devotional. For a while I melted into that devotional atmosphere, but because of trouble with my back I could not sit for long. After about ten minutes I softly said to Hiteshbhai, 'I cannot sit cross legged for long, so I will sit on the steps of the hall.' He agreed with a smile. I came out of the hall. The cleanliness and discipline of the grounds outside were amazing. Volunteers stood on their feet keeping watch over them. I had seen the same cleanliness and discipline at the Kaaba Sharif in Mecca and the Masjid an Nabawi in Medina. I was sitting on the steps of the hall when my eyes fell on my friend Brahmbhatt. We greeted each other with 'Jai Swaminarayan'.

'Mehboobbhai! What brings you here?' he said, staring at me in surprise. Sensing his surprise, I said, 'In the month of Ramadan one should visit a holy place, shouldn't one!' And he welcomed my answer with a smile. In the course of conversation I said, 'I wish to have darshan of Pramukh Swami.'
He said, 'You see those curtains over there! Come there after the bhajan programme.'

When the bhajan programme was over, I stepped in that direction. Brahmbhatt was standing there with a pass for me. Giving me the pass, he said, 'This pass is to go into Swamiji's room. Inside, the volunteers will guide you.' And I gazed at him with gratitude. As soon as I entered the room, I was first checked. Then I was asked to fill in a form. When I had filled in the form and handed it over, my hands were cleaned with disinfectant. After all this care, I entered the room with a pounding heart. Ninety year old Pramukh Swamiji was sitting in a fully modern wheelchair. Gliding along in the wheelchair, he was giving everyone his blessings. When my turn came, I bowed to him and said, 'My name is Professor Mehboob Desai. In the holy month of Ramadan I have come for the darshan and blessings of a great soul.'

At my introduction, a smile spread across Pramukh Swami's face. Touching my shoulder, he said something in a very soft voice. I did not hear his words properly. Thinking that the blessing was complete, I began to walk away. Then Pramukh Swami raised his hand, called me back and said in an audible voice, 'Be very happy. Be prosperous and do a great deal of work for society.'

The devotees around watched this shower of blessings in astonishment. They were mostly not used to such an event, because Pramukh Swami never calls a visitor back to say something. Moreover, his health was not good at that time. Even so, by showering smiling blessings on a Muslim, Pramukh Swami embodied the simplicity of a great soul. When I came out joyfully with this prasad of his, my heart was overflowing with the abundant blessings of a great soul that I had received so unexpectedly."

There was a letter from a youth. He had been in love with a girl, but the girl had betrayed him and left him. In the letter he had written, "Please bless me that I get that same girl back. At the moment I have become addicted."

Pramukh Swami Maharaj had a phone call put through to the youth and explained to him, "What has happened now has happened for the good. It ended right here. If she had betrayed you like this after marriage, there would have been great trouble."

Then Swamishri said, "If you do puja and apply the tilak chandlo, you will feel ashamed to do anything wrong. You will feel in your mind, 'I cannot do such a thing.' If you wear the tilak chandlo, your addictions will also go."
The youth said, "I cannot forget her."
Swamishri said, "We will pray that you forget everything and find peace."

Today Pramukh Swami Maharaj gave a wonderful blessing in the sadhus' assembly. Various sadhus who had been in Swamishri's company described incidents they had seen with their own eyes in which they had experienced Swamishri's virtues.

Ghanshyamcharan Swami spoke about one incident: "In the village of Kundhada near Bhavnagar, Swamishri gave blessings until 12:30 at night. Even though it had become so late, Swamishri's faith was unshaken."

Explaining how such a feeling can remain constantly, Swamishri said, "Since the time of Shriji Maharaj, whether the sadhus are travelling in the villages or are in the mandir, they have a love for katha. Gunatitanand Swami too never let katha come to a halt. Bhagatji Maharaj also gave talks. Shastriji Maharaj gave talks in such a way that one did not know where the time went in katha. And Jogi Maharaj was something else altogether; his katha was always going on, the akhada (training ground) of satsang was always going on. The potter's akhada, the blacksmith's akhada, the carpenter's and the wrestler's akhada are all busy pleasing the world. In the same way we want to please God, so the akhada of katha should be kept going. And truly, in our Gunatit knowledge the akhada does go on. It began with Shriji Maharaj and has always continued. When Shastriji Maharaj bathed at eleven at night and sat down to do katha, it would be two or three in the morning. He too had such a great desire to explain this knowledge and these talks to others; such was his passion. As for Jogi Maharaj, whether there were small children, elders or an assembly, his katha was always going on, and he spoke with humour and joy. So we too should not be lazy in katha, kirtan and bhajan. If we are lazy in that, then no virtues will come in us, and we will not get strength either. Through katha we get strength, and we get peace and happiness. Our aim is to do whatever little we can from the way they have taught. Through katha we get strength and we benefit.

There should be no laziness or carelessness at all in katha and bhajan. A few sanskars (good impressions) have formed, and we cannot do as much as they did, but whatever we do is useful in pleasing God."

In a village in Gujarat, Pramukh Swami Maharaj had given up his morning walk and gone to 40 homes in the village for padharamanis. It had only been a year since Swamishri's heart attack, yet Swamishri kept everyone happy in this way. Similarly, in a village in Saurashtra, Swamishri was taking his walk at one house, but to please a devotee, he left the walk halfway, went to where that devotee had made arrangements, and completed the rest of his walk there. The sadhus told of these incidents from his earlier travels.

From these incidents, Atmatrupt Swami asked Swamishri a question: "Swami Bapa! When we hear so many such incidents, one thing is certainly seen, that you have always had only one thought: how can the devotees be pleased? For that you have never thought of your own convenience. Many times the devotees insist on impractical things, yet you have always tried only to look after the devotees. You have never looked at their natures. So what is the reason behind such a feeling of yours?"

Swamishri said, "Our Sampradaya is woven through and through with devotees and sadhus. If the devotees are happy, everything becomes favourable for us. Then even if we have a little trouble or difficulty, padharamanis go on so that they are pleased. Shastriji Maharaj also went everywhere for padharamanis. Even when his health was poor he did padharamanis. He never did anything that would displease a devotee. If a devotee is happy, then first of all he will have satsang, and his soul will benefit. So when there are padharamanis or such occasions, one has to go without counting comfort or discomfort.

In Manavadar, Shastriji Maharaj's health was not good, yet because of the devotees' insistence he went for padharamanis. He went lying down in a bullock cart, and the devotees were pleased. If devotees are not displeased and not hurt, satsang stays in their souls and Thakorji's seva goes on. We may face hardship, but without looking at the body, the feeling was how satsang could grow and how this conviction could be established. Even when Jogi Maharaj's health was poor, he went for padharamanis. Even where some people would not take to satsang, he would still go to their homes. If we go, one day their mind will become good, and if they see virtue, it will be good. Whether they developed conviction and understanding or not, he insisted on going for padharamanis. Shastriji Maharaj and Jogi Maharaj have gone everywhere.

How satsang could grow and how everyone in satsang could develop conviction in Akshar Purushottam was very much in the minds of Shastriji Maharaj and Jogi Maharaj. By talking and talking, they made people's conviction firm. Such was their effort and their firmness that this conviction would certainly come. We might think, 'If it is to happen it will happen, otherwise let it rest, why take all this trouble?' Our minds may become like that. And there are also people who pull us back. But they did not look at that, they did not look to the body's comfort, but only to one thing: how conviction in Akshar Purushottam could come! How this knowledge could be understood! For that they kept the devotees' feelings in mind, the devotees developed such conviction, and today this satsang exists only through their wish. Through Jogi Bapa's wish all these sadhus came. At present all the sadhus are travelling in the villages, which is very good.

Reports keep coming of the sadhus travelling in the villages. Whoever travels, gets nourished. Swami travelled, and that is why our satsang has grown so much today. And so much seva and so many mandirs, how did they come about? Through the sadhus' travels and the sadhus' talks. In this way they laid deep roots. So, thinking of what they did, we should do as much as we can. We cannot do as much as they did, but if we behave according to the commands they gave, everything will happen. If our principles of niyam and dharma, agna and upasana, goodwill and loyalty are in our souls, there is strength. We have heard their words and their katha, and from them we too have received strength. Jogi Maharaj still wants to make satsang grow a great deal. The universes are to be filled. He used to say, 'I want to colour Mumbai, I want to colour Africa.' When he said it, we could not believe it, but today we see that it has been coloured. Only through his wish has satsang grown so much abroad. His wish had that much strength. The children's mandal, youth mandal, kishore mandal, elders' mandal and satsang mandal are also his wishes, and we see that his wish has that much strength. Does anyone find it easy to become a sadhu?
'Why join the Swaminarayans, where one must rise and bathe every day;
We will not join them, we prefer to eat without bathing.'

In such religions it is easy, nothing has to be done, but here one has to control the senses and increase the strength of conviction, and all of that is difficult. The work goes on by keeping those principles, and when the sadhus travel, people benefit and mandirs are built. Because it is his wish, mandirs are built and the knowledge of Akshar Purushottam spreads. Our work goes on through his strength. So on the path he has given, we should make sure that katha, kirtan and bhajan go on. Because there is unity, friendliness and oneness, things are going very well and will continue to."

Pramukh Swami Maharaj was in the city of San Jose in America. Here, during the meetings, a devotee unknowingly came carrying a small girl. As soon as the volunteer noticed, the girl was moved away, but Swamishri had a doubt, so after that he refused even to take water to swallow his medicine. Narayancharan Swami told this incident of Swamishri's firmness in the panch vartman (the five vows).

To draw inspiration from this incident, Atmatrupt Swami asked Swamishri a question: "Bapa! In this incident the girl had not even touched you, yet you felt such unease and concern, and insisted on fasting right to the end. So what was your thought behind such insistence?"

Swamishri said, "This insistence has been there through the tradition. Renouncing wealth and women is a great command for a renunciant, it is Shriji Maharaj's command. Shastriji Maharaj also faced such situations many times, but he would not give way at all. Jogi Maharaj also insisted on it. If there was even a slight brush, he would say, 'Let us just fast.' For a sadhu, wealth and women are called the two great vows. Since we have become sadhus, there should never be any contact with women and never any contact with wealth. If we keep things as our own, then they become a bondage. In satsang everyone gets all facilities, so there is no need for us to keep anything. Shriji Maharaj's main command is that if we have become sadhus, we must keep renunciation of wealth and women. We have seen that insistence, so we too should have that insistence. We want to please them, don't we!
'His way is our way, any other way is a hindrance.'

They were great personalities, they liberated countless souls and had such power, yet they took great care that not even the slightest command of Shriji Maharaj was broken. And because they lived like that, we have received a little strength. The very first dharma of a sadhu is the renunciation of wealth and women.

Why has satsang grown? Because of niyam and dharma, agna, upasana, loyalty, the renunciation of wealth and women, unity, friendliness and oneness. If we observe these properly, we will have peace, peace and peace. These rules have not been made just for the sake of making them, but for the liberation of the soul. Our liberation happens, and the liberation of those we teach also happens. They become firm that the sadhus are very good and behave according to Shriji Maharaj's commands. When people see virtue, satsang grows. By being insistent, satsang grows, the soul has peace, we also have strength, and God is pleased. We have to do everything so that the great ones are pleased. They have done it and shown us that this can be done, that it is not impossible. Our forefathers have done it. So keep firmness in niyam and dharma."
A father had come with his son. This father, who was well off, complained about his son and said, "He has every comfort, but he keeps having thoughts of committing suicide."

Explaining to the young man, Pramukh Swami Maharaj said, "Put the thought of suicide out of your mind. Whatever your business, work or farming is, do it well. Pray to God. Everything will be fine, so do not think of suicide."

Pramukh Swami Maharaj had had a heart attack. After that he was resting at the premises of Shri Ashokbhai Patel, the owner of 'Aims Oxygen' in Vadodara. During those days came the fast of Chaitra sud 9 (Ram Navmi). On this day too Swamishri fasted the whole day without taking even a drop of water. He even hesitated to take his medicine. Narayanmuni Swami told this incident. To draw inspiration from Swamishri's firmness, Atmatrupt Swami asked Swamishri a question.
Atmatrupt Swami said, "You do not need to do anything, yet in such a condition you insisted on fasting like this. What was your feeling behind it?"

Swamishri said, "The feeling is that we are not to look at the body, we are to look at the atma. But we think only of the body, and when we think of the body, our thoughts become weak. It is Shriji Maharaj's command, and if there is a keenness to obey that command, everything happens. I have seen incidents of Shastriji Maharaj and Jogi Maharaj, how even when they were ill they did not look to the body's comfort. Even if the doctor advised otherwise, they would somehow observe the fast. If others see even a little of what they did, they get inspiration. The great ones also behave in a certain way to inspire others. Nothing would affect them, yet they behave so that others' conduct does not slacken. If one's own conduct is right, others get inspiration. The reason they insisted was not to increase their own greatness or importance, but because it is Shriji Maharaj's command and so that others get good inspiration. There was nothing at all for their own comfort. They did not do anything for that, nor do they. They always disregarded the body, so they never spoke of anything lax and never let anything lax happen. They behaved strictly, and that too was for the benefit of others. Otherwise they are always happy. They have God's command, upasana, firmness, everything, yet this is so that other souls may be benefited. So we should draw inspiration from them and do all this."

ds.t: Stepping out for a phone call
w: Pramukh Swami Maharaj was in the town of Daytona Beach in America. He was sitting with the sadhus. An important phone call came there. As the important matter had to be discussed alone, Swamishri himself got up and went outside, but did not ask the sadhus to get up. Brahmadarshan Swami told of this incident.

He asked Swamishri, "All of us sadhus are your disciples, and it is our duty to look after your convenience, yet you chose to get up and go outside yourself, and thought that the sadhus should not have to go out. So how do you constantly have such regard for the sadhus?"

Swamishri said, "On such an occasion, rather than making ten people get up, what is wrong if we ourselves get up, go outside and talk? If it is about someone, others may think, 'Is this devotee like this?' So all this is the way of satsang. Shriji Maharaj and Shastriji Maharaj also used to talk in that way. If we get up, go outside and talk, others will not be put out, will not feel bad and will not see faults. So the great ones have done everything in that way. The more we look to that, the happier we will be."

The invitation card for the installation of murtis in the assembly hall at Manavadar was given to Pramukh Swami Maharaj. It said, "On the sacred land of Manavadar, the mandir is being built with the blessings of Pramukh Swami Maharaj."

Reading this, Swamishri said, "Shastriji Maharaj and Yogiji Maharaj travelled so much in Manavadar! Their names should be written, shouldn't they! Even when Shastriji Maharaj's health was not good, he had a bullock cart brought and, lying down in the cart, he personally went to devotees' homes."

Jagmal Pithiya, who had come from Vadodara, had so far brought 176 men and women devotees into satsang. He had come with a list of all their names. He said to Pramukh Swami Maharaj, "Please place your hand on this paper, so that satsang takes root in all their souls."
Pleased, Swamishri placed his hand on the list and in this way blessed them all.

ds.t: Give up the thought of suicide
w: A father had brought his son. This father, who was well off, complained about his son, "We are happy in every way, but he keeps having thoughts of suicide."

Explaining to the young man, Pramukh Swami Maharaj said, "Put the thought of suicide out of your mind. Whatever business or farming you have, do it well. Pray to Bhagwan. Everything will be fine, so do not think of suicide."

ds.t: It is good it ended now
w: There was a letter from a youth. He had been in love with a girl, but the girl had betrayed him and left him. In the letter he had written, "Bless me so that I get that same girl back. Right now I have become an addict."

Pramukh Swami Maharaj had a call put through to the youth and, explaining to him, said, "Whatever has happened now has happened for the good. It ended right here. If she had betrayed you like this after marriage, there would have been great difficulty."

Then Swamishri said, "If you do puja and apply tilak and chandlo, you will feel ashamed to do wrong. You will think, 'I cannot do such a thing.' If you have tilak and chandlo, your addiction will also go."
The youth said, "I cannot forget her."
Swamishri said, "We will pray that you forget everything and find peace."

In a village in Gujarat, Pramukh Swami Maharaj had given up his morning walk and visited 40 homes in the village. It was only a year since Swamishri had had a heart attack, yet Swamishri kept everyone happy in this way. Similarly, in a village in Saurashtra, Swamishri was taking his walk at one home, but to please a devotee he left half his walk and went to the place that devotee had arranged, and completed the rest of his walk there. The sants told of these incidents from his earlier travels.

From these incidents, Atmatrupt Swami asked Swamishri a question, "Swami Bapa! When we hear many such incidents, one thing is clearly seen: you have always had only one thought, how can the devotees be pleased? For that you have never thought of your own convenience. Many times the devotees have an impractical insistence, yet you have always tried to look after the devotees. You have never looked at their natures. What is the reason behind this feeling of yours?"

Swamishri said, "Our Sampradaya is woven through with devotees and sants. If the devotees are happy, everything becomes favourable for us. Even if we then face a little hardship or difficulty, the work of padhramanis goes on so that they are pleased. Shastriji Maharaj too did padhramanis everywhere. Even when his health was poor, he would do padhramanis. He did nothing that would displease a devotee. If a devotee remains happy, first of all he takes up satsang, and his soul benefits. So when there are padhramanis or such occasions, one has to go without counting convenience or inconvenience.

In Manavadar, Shastriji Maharaj's health was not good, yet because they insisted, he went for a padhramani, lying down in a bullock cart, and the devotees were pleased. If devotees are not displeased and not hurt, satsang remains in their soul and Thakorji's seva is done. We may suffer hardship, but the feeling was, not looking at the body, how can satsang grow, how can this conviction take root. Even when Jogi Maharaj's health was weak, he would go for padhramanis. Even if some did not take to satsang, he would still go to their homes. If we go, one day their mind will improve, and if they see virtue, it will be good. Whether or not they developed conviction and understanding, he insisted on going for padhramanis. Shastriji Maharaj and Jogi Maharaj went everywhere.

How the satsang could grow, and how everyone in satsang could have conviction in Akshar-Purushottam, was very much in the minds of Shastriji Maharaj and Jogi Maharaj. By talking and talking, they made people's conviction firm. Such was their effort and their firmness that this conviction would certainly take root. We might think, 'If it is to happen it will happen, otherwise let it rest, why go to all this trouble?' Our mind might become like that. And there are also those who hold us back. But they never looked at that, they never looked at the comfort of the body, but only at one thing, how could conviction in Akshar-Purushottam take root! How could this knowledge be understood! That is why they took care of the devotees' feelings, and the devotees developed such conviction, and today this satsang exists only by their wish. By Jogi Bapa's wish, all these sadhus were made. Now all the sants travel in the villages, and it is very good.

Reports are coming in from all the sants travelling in the villages. The one who roams, grazes. Because Swami travelled, our satsang has grown so much today, and so much seva, so many mandirs, how did all that happen? Through the sants travelling, through the sants' talks. In this way they laid deep roots. So thinking of what they did, we should do as much as we can. We will not be able to do as much as they did, but if we act according to the commands they gave, everything will be done. If our niyams and dharma, obedience and upasana, goodwill and loyalty, these principles, are in our souls, we have strength. We have heard their words and their katha, and from that we too have received strength. Jogi Maharaj still wants to make the satsang grow much more. The universes are to be filled. He used to say, 'I want to colour Mumbai, I want to colour Africa.' When he said it, we could not believe it, but today we see that it has been coloured. By his wish alone the satsang has grown so much abroad. There was so much strength in his wish. The children's groups, youth groups, teenagers' groups, elders' groups and satsang groups are also his wishes, and we see how much strength there is in his wish. Does anyone find it easy to become a sadhu?
'Why join the Swaminarayans, where one must bathe every day on rising;
Rather join the free and easy ones, where one may eat without bathing.'

In such faiths there is fun, nothing has to be done, but here one has to control the senses and increase the strength of conviction, and all of that is difficult. Keeping those principles, the work gets done, and as the sants travel, people benefit and mandirs are built. Because it is his wish, mandirs are built and the knowledge of Akshar-Purushottam grows. Our work goes on by their strength. So on the path they have given us, we should see that katha, kirtans and bhajan go on. Because there is unity, friendliness and oneness, things go very well and will go well."

Pramukh Swami Maharaj was in the city of San Jose in America. During the meetings here, a devotee unknowingly brought a little girl in his arms. As soon as a volunteer noticed, the girl was moved away, but Swamishri had a doubt, so after that he even refused to take water to swallow his medicine. Narayancharan Swami told of this incident showing Swamishri's firmness in the five vows.

To draw inspiration from this incident, Atmatrupt Swami asked Swamishri a question, "Bapa! In this incident the girl had not even touched you, yet you felt such concern and anxiety, and insisted on fasting right to the end. What was your thought behind such insistence?"

Swamishri said, "This insistence has come down through the tradition. Renunciation of wealth and women is a major command for renunciants, it is Shriji Maharaj's command. Shastriji Maharaj too faced such incidents many times, but he never gave in. Jogi Maharaj also insisted on it. If there was even a slight brush, he would say, 'Let us just fast.' For a sadhu, wealth and women are the two major vows. Since we have become sadhus, there should never be any contact with women and never any contact with wealth. If we keep anything as our own, it then becomes a bondage. In satsang everyone gets facilities, so there is no need for us to keep anything. Shriji Maharaj's main command is that one who has become a sadhu should renounce wealth and women. I saw that insistence, so we too keep that insistence. We want to please them, don't we!
'Their way is our way; any other way is a hindrance.'

They were great souls, they liberated many souls, they had such power, yet they took great care that not even the slightest of Shriji Maharaj's commands was broken. And because they lived like that, we have received a little strength. The very first dharma of a sadhu is renunciation of wealth and women.

Why has the satsang grown? Niyams and dharma, obedience to commands, upasana, loyalty, renunciation of wealth and women, unity, friendliness and oneness. If we follow these properly, we will have peace, peace and peace. These niyams have not been made just for the sake of it, but for the liberation of the soul. We are liberated, and those we preach to are also liberated, and they become firm in the conviction that the sadhus are very good and act according to Shriji Maharaj's commands. When people see virtue, the satsang grows. By insisting on these, satsang also grows, there is peace in the soul, we have strength, and Bhagwan is pleased. We have to do everything to please the great soul. They have done it and shown us that this can be done, it is not impossible. Our forefathers did it. So keep firm in the niyams and dharma."

Pramukh Swami Maharaj had suffered a heart attack. After that he was resting at the premises of Shri Ashokbhai Patel, owner of "Aims Oxygen", in Vadodara. During these days came the fast of Chaitra sud 9 (Ram Navami). Even on this day Swamishri fasted the whole day without taking even a drop of water. He was even reluctant to take his medicines. Narayanmuni Swami told of this incident. To draw inspiration from such firmness of Swamishri, Atmatrupt Swami asked Swamishri a question.
Atmatrupt Swami: "You do not need to do anything, yet in such a condition you insisted on such a fast. What feeling lay behind it?"

Swamishri said, "The feeling is that we are not to look at the body, we are to look at the atma, but we think only of the body, and when we think of the body, our thoughts become weak. It is Shriji Maharaj's command, and if we are intent on following that command, everything happens. I have seen incidents of Shastriji Maharaj and Jogi Maharaj, how even when they were ill they did not look to the comfort of the body. Even when the doctor advised otherwise, they would somehow keep the fast. If others see even a little of what they did, they get inspiration. Great souls act in a certain way for the inspiration of others too. They themselves would face no problem, but they act this way so that others' conduct does not slacken. If one's own conduct is right, others get inspiration. The reason they insisted was not to increase their greatness or importance, but because it is Shriji Maharaj's command and so that others get good inspiration. There is nothing for their own comfort at all. They never did it and they do not do it. They had only disregard for the body, so they never spoke a weak word or let it happen. They behaved strictly, and that too was for the benefit of others. Otherwise they are happy anyway. They already have obedience to Bhagwan's commands, upasana and firmness, yet this is so that others' souls may benefit. So drawing inspiration from them, we should do all this."

ds.t: Rather than make ten stand up
w: Pramukh Swami Maharaj was in the town of Daytona Beach in America. He was sitting with the sants. An important phone call came. Since the important matter had to be discussed alone, Swamishri himself got up and went out, but did not ask the sants to get up. Brahmadarshan Swami told of this incident.

He asked Swamishri, "All of us sants are your disciples and it is our duty to see to your convenience, yet you chose to get up yourself and go out, and you thought that the sants should not have to go out. How do you always keep such a sense of the glory of the sants?"

Swamishri said, "On such an occasion, rather than make ten people stand up, what is wrong with getting up ourselves, going out and talking? If someone has such a matter, others might think, is this devotee like this? So all of that is the way of satsang. Shriji Maharaj and Shastriji Maharaj also talked in this way. If we get up, go out and talk, the other person does not feel upset, does not feel bad, and does not see faults. That is how the great ones did everything. The more we look to that, the happier we will be."

The invitation card for the installation of murtis in the assembly hall at Manavadar was given to Pramukh Swami Maharaj. It said, "A mandir is being built in the sanctified land of Manavadar with the blessings of Pramukh Swami Maharaj."

Reading this, Swamishri said, "Shastriji Maharaj and Yogiji Maharaj travelled so much in Manavadar! Their names should be written, shouldn't they! Even when Shastriji Maharaj's health was not good, he sent for a bullock cart and, lying down in the cart, went himself to visit devotees' homes."

Today Mahant Swami Maharaj came up to the mandir for the evening arti. After the arti, during the singing of the ashtak, when the attendants asked him to sit, he said, "I have sat enough in my room. Here let us stand before Thakorji."
Everyone saw his devotion standing firm on its feet even at 83.
After the ashtak, he was asked to sit on a chair in the entrance hall for manasi. Swamishri refused that too, and sat cross legged right on the floor near Ghanshyam Maharaj's shrine for manasi.
A devotee came to meet Mahant Swami Maharaj with his two sons. He and the young men said, "Whichever one you say is ready to become a sadhu. You choose."
Swamishri began to laugh. He would not give a decision...
So the sadhus said, "Both of you bow your heads. Swami will place his hand on the head of whichever one he wishes..."
Both bowed their heads, and Swamishri placed his hands on both their heads. Everyone burst out laughing. Swamishri wishes to make sadhus of all who are suited for it...
Today, when Mahant Swami Maharaj sat on his bed to go to sleep, there was talk about how early Swamishri wakes up. Swamishri said, "The earliest I have done puja is at 5.28."
The sadhus asked, "In the room? Here?"
Swamishri said, "No, outside, in America..."
On checking, it was found that Swamishri had said it exactly right. The date was 8 July 2017, the place was Chicago. When Swamishri sat for puja, the clock showed 5.28.
He remembers at what time he did his very earliest puja!! How many such things must be imprinted on his memory every day!!
